$comment: The scope object of spec §13j. Set by the field's experts, not by the agent and not by the owner. Versioned: a change here is a change to what the agent may work on.
principle: a projection is a line integral of attenuation and its noise is photon statistics; dose is photon count

set_by.$comment: roles, never names — naming a person in a design document commits them to something they have not agreed to. `named` is filled when a panel exists.

in.boundary: angular undersampling — the reconstruction problem, not the acquisition hardware that would allow it
restricted angular range, including the geometries a scanner cannot physically complete
the new detector class, re-evaluated rather than assumed
spectral separation into material bases — the decomposition and its noise, not the clinical reading of it
what a protocol actually delivered, in photon terms, so that two scanners' '50%' can be compared
detectability rather than fidelity — the field's rung 1

out.question: diagnostic performance
out.why: image quality is not diagnostic performance

out.question: scanner hardware design
out.why: it evaluates detectors and does not design them

out.question: protocol decisions for a patient
out.why: a dose choice for a person is a clinical act

claims_allowed: reconstruction quality at a stated dose
detectability under a stated task and observer
claims_forbidden: any claim about a named individual
any statement that a result is clinically actionable without the endpoint role's sign-off
would_move_the_boundary: photon-counting reducing dose enough at acquisition that reconstruction is no longer where the problem is — contraction toward task-based assessment
$watch_comment: if this rung stays blocked by a dependency the scope put out of bounds, the boundary is in the wrong place (§13j)
